subject: [PATCH 02/22] mm: publish and clear node memory states via helpers

2026-11-14.patch_summary: This patch centralizes the updates of node memory states by introducing two new functions, `node_set_memory_state` and `node_clear_memory_state`, which replace the separate calls to set and clear individual state flags in various places throughout the code. The behavior remains unchanged, but the code is simplified and easier to maintain. The patch also removes redundant checks for high and normal memory states, making it more efficient.

reviews.author: Richard Cheng
reviews.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng noted that the patch introduces additional cache pressure due to up to three set_bit() calls on node_states[], which is __read_mostly, and suggested adding a test-before-set in the helper or addressing this in the commit message.
reviews.raw_body:
Um, so I am not sure how much cache pressure this will add, I assume it's small ?

Just want to point out that the old code only wrote these bits for a node's first
memory. THis now does up to 3 set_bit() calls on node_states[] for every onlined block.
The result is the same, but node_states[] is __read_mostly. A test-before-set in the helper
would keep the old behavior, or if you would like to keep it, please address in commit message.

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that setting N_MEMORY in hotplug code could lead to a race condition, agreed to add a test before setting new state and early-out if necessary.
reviews.raw_body:
Hotplug isn't on a particular hot path, but I can test N_MEMORY before
setting any new state and just early-out.  That would keep the behavior.

-- 
~Gregory

2026-11-18.patch_summary: This patch centralizes the updates of node memory states in Linux kernel by introducing two new functions, `node_set_memory_state` and `node_clear_memory_state`, which replace the existing separate calls to set or clear individual memory states (N_MEMORY, N_NORMAL_MEMORY, and N_HIGH_MEMORY). The behavior remains unchanged. This change aims to simplify the code and make it more maintainable.
